newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Mulia sees 180 bln rph 1997 profit, up 57 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Mulia sees 180 bln rph 1997 profit, up 57 pct.

text.p: Indonesian glass and tile manufacturer PT Mulia Industrindo said on Friday the company is looking for a 57 percent increase in net profit in 1997 despite a fall in float glass prices in international markets.
"We expect to book a net profit of 180 billion rupiah (US$77.4 million) or a 57 percent growth from our 1996 net profit target," Mulia investor relations director Rony Djohan told Reuters.
He said the company expected to meet the target despite a drop in prices of float glass on international markets as Mulia had implemented new strategies.
"Since float glass prices began falling, we have changed some of our business expansion and strategies by increasing ceramics' contribution from mid-1996," he added.

He said Mulia had raised the sales revenue target of the ceramics division to 48 percent of total sales from the second half of this year from an average of about 41 percent since 1995. The contribution of float glass to total sales has been cut to 38 percent from 43 percent.
Djohan said the company also lowered its container glass production goal to 14 percent from 16 percent.
"For 1997, we are targeting 57 percent sales contribution from ceramic products, 38 percent from float glass and 12 percent from container glass," he added.
He said the new strategy would offset losses from the glass division as demand for ceramics in the domestic market was growing rapidly.
Djohan also said he believed that the move would improve company earnings and investor confidence in the firm.
"Some investors still think that Mulia Industrindo only produces glass but ceramics is also a major contributor to company earnings," he added.

He said the company planned to increase ceramics production capacity to 150,000 square metres per day in 1997 from the current 92,000 square metres when two new plants come onstream by the end of this year and a third is built in 1997.
But Djohan said Mulia's first quarter 1996 net profit forecast had to be revised downwards to 115 billion rupiah from 130 billion due to a fall in glass prices.
Market consensus in September for Mulia's net profit for 1996 is 121 billion rupiah and 161.4 billion rupiah for next year.
Djohan said that the average selling price of float glass had dropped to US$370 per tonne in the first half of this year from US$380 in 1995. He said the current price was US$325.
"So, if we do not change strategies, our earnings will be impacted," he added.
